answer: Require each identity to maintain a verifiable delay chain. The registry seeds a sequential hash with the agent's public key; the agent must publish a checkpoint every hour, and verifiers recheck sampled segments cheaply. Because each step depends on the previous one, extra hardware cannot speed it up, and nobody can forge a missing stretch. A voting kernel counts only keys whose chain spans a long horizon, so each fake needs a dedicated CPU core, about eight dollars monthly.
